children: Singapore's Aster Chemicals and Energy has bought crude oil from the Americas and Africa to replace part of its Middle Eastern supply after the Iran war disrupted Gulf exports, an executive said on Wednesday.

The refiner used to buy 70% of its crude from the Middle East and has pivoted to West Africa, Latin America, the United States, and Canada for supplies, Han Lih Kwong, senior general manager at Aster, told the APPEC conference.
Aster, a joint venture between Indonesia's Chandra Asri and trading major Glencore, operates a 237,000 barrel-per-day refinery on Singapore's Bukom Island.
